- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5–10% spike) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use sentiment to dampen momentum.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider pulling back.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment; weight recent 5–7 days more heavily if sentiment is volatile.
- If true outcome is below forecast by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid further overcorrection.
